correctness.rationale: Fourier diagonalization gives eigenvalues 2,±sqrt(2),0,−2 and distance-class amplitudes u0=(X+1+2C)/4, u1=i(Y+sqrt(2)D)/4, u2=(X−1)/4, u3=i(Y−sqrt(2)D)/4,u4=(X+1−2C)/4. Independently calculated rational moments of density (1−cos(alpha)/2)(1−cos(2beta))/(2pi)^2: E X=−1/4, E X²=1/2, E C²=1/4, E D²=3/4, E Y=E D=0; all five mean class probabilities exactly 1/8. This law has full torus support (zero density on a measure-zero set only), so uniform target lies in relative interior of compact phase-image convex hull. Because ratio of 2 and sqrt(2) is irrational, every t>T phase tail is dense; the elementary relative-interior convex-density lemma gives an EXACT finite convex combination from physical times. A single affine normalization reduces dimension ≤4, hence Caratheodory gives ≤5 positive weights and distinct times. The C8 distance-two uniformity condition and p0=p4 show no single time is uniform; Cesaro p2=3/32. Independent exact moment algebra checked; the existence proof rests on convex geometry, not approximate numerical sampling.
